findings.title: The reader thread keeps running forever if a delete throws.
findings.body: `deletedAll.set(true)` only runs if every `remove()` call succeeds. If one delete throws (for example a 404 or a server error), the test fails but the reader thread keeps calling the admin API in a tight loop until the JVM exits. That load and noise spill into every later test. Put `deletedAll.set(true)` in a `finally` block, then join the thread. Making it a daemon thread would also help.

findings.title: The test checks for errors without waiting for the reader thread to finish.
findings.body: `deletedAll.set(true)` is followed straight away by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, empty())`. The reader thread may still be inside `groups(...)` at that moment. If its last request fails, which is the request most likely to hit the half-deleted state, the exception is added after the assertion has already passed. The test then passes even though the error it is meant to catch happened. Keep a reference to the thread and call `join()` (with a timeout) before asserting.

findings.title: Groups created so far are left in the shared realm if creation fails partway.
findings.body: If `fail(...)` is hit partway through the creation loop, the groups already created are never deleted. They stay in the realm that the other `GroupTest` methods share, which can break tests that count or list groups. Delete the created groups in a `finally` block, or register them for cleanup through the managed realm.
